title: Osteogenic Stimulators

criteria.text: Electrical: nonunion only after >= 6 months without healing
criteria.span: nonunion of long bone fractures is considered to exist only after 6 or more months have elapsed without healing of the fracture.

criteria.text: Electrical: serial radiographs, >= 2 sets with multiple views, >= 90 days apart, showing healing ceased >= 3 months
criteria.span: Serial radiographs must include a minimum of 2 sets of radiographs, each including multiple views of the fracture site, separated by a minimum of 90 days.

criteria.text: Noninvasive electrical: failed fusion with >= 9 months since last surgery
criteria.span: Failed fusion, where a minimum of 9 months has elapsed since the last surgery;

criteria.text: Electrical adjunct to spinal fusion: prior failed fusion at the same site, or multilevel fusion of >= 3 vertebrae
criteria.span: as an adjunct to spinal fusion surgery for patients at high risk of pseudarthrosis due to previously failed spinal fusion at the same site or for those undergoing multiple level fusion. A multiple level fusion involves 3 or more vertebrae

criteria.text: Invasive (implantable) stimulator covered only for long bone nonunion and spinal fusion adjunct
criteria.span: The invasive stimulator device is covered only for the following indications:

criteria.text: Ultrasonic: >= 2 radiograph sets >= 90 days apart, multiple views, with physician written interpretation of no healing
criteria.span: Each radiograph set must include multiple views of the fracture site accompanied with a written interpretation by a physician stating that there has been no clinically significant evidence of fracture healing between the 2 sets of radiographs

criteria.text: Exclusion: nonunion of skull, vertebrae, or tumor-related
criteria.span: Nonunion fractures of the skull, vertebrae and those that are tumor-related are excluded from coverage.

criteria.text: Ultrasonic not used concurrently with other non-invasive osteogenic devices
criteria.span: Ultrasonic osteogenic stimulators may not be used concurrently with other non-invasive osteogenic devices.

criteria.text: Ultrasonic prior to surgical intervention is covered (2005)
criteria.span: noninvasive ultrasound stimulation for the treatment of nonunion bone fractures prior to surgical intervention is reasonable and necessary

notes: Electrical nonunion = >= 6 months without healing AND serial radiographs (>= 2 sets, multiple views, >= 90 days apart) showing healing ceased >= 3 months. Ultrasonic: since April 2005 a prior failed surgery is not required, and the NCD does not limit ultrasonic coverage to long bones. Ambiguity for expert review: the skull/vertebrae/tumor-related exclusion sits in the ultrasonic section's Non-Covered list; it is tested only with an ultrasonic device here. Failed-fusion and congenital pseudarthrosis indications appear only under the noninvasive electrical device.
